label: first copy step (echoing the first original token) in long sequences, favoring certain first tokens
explanation: Fires almost only on the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx==1: input is the fed-back first original token, output is the second); 94% of activations and 97% of mass are there. It never fires in the original phase, rarely on <DEL> itself (2% of mass), and essentially never after recall_idx 2. Firing rate and magnitude increase steeply with sequence length (L=9 holds 67% of mass, L=8 22%, L<=6 under 3%), and depend on the identity of the first token: b fires most (4.6x lift, the top activations are mostly b-initial L=9 sequences), followed by z, h, u, e, 0, f, w, k, s, 1, r; tokens like l, g, i, t rarely fire. The boolean cut (recall_idx==1, L>=8, first token in the favored set) gets dev F1 0.59 / mass recall 0.72. The simpler recall_idx==1 & L>=8 gets F1 0.45 / mass 0.86. Activation looks like a graded combination of length and first-token identity, so no clean threshold captures it.
